Now I understand. The entrypoint:
1. Checks /models/.initialized or /models/diarization.generated.yaml - if either missing, download.
2. `python -m shared.model_download required-models.txt -gr` — the model_download script exits(1) on failure. Since pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1 is gated and requires an accepted user agreement + valid token, the download failed -> exit(1). But `.initialized` was touched anyway (the mv and touch lines are after, but since the script exited... wait). Actually the entrypoint has no `set -e`, so even if python exits 1, the subsequent lines run: `mv /app/diarization.generated.yaml /models/` (fails, no file), `touch /models/.initialized` runs and creates .initialized. Then `python -m asr_service` runs.

So .initialized exists from the bootstrap despite download failure. The diarization.generated.yaml was never generated. That's why the diarization model_path points to /models/diarization.generated.yaml which doesn't exist, and Pipeline.from_pretrained interprets it as a repo id -> error.

So the root cause: no valid HF token supplied (placeholder). The guide explicitly requires a real HF token. Also, pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1 is a gated model requiring user acceptance.
